items.hook: World War II: A German submarine makes the first attack of the war against a United States warship, the USS Greer.
items.body: USS Greer (DD–145) was a Wickes-class destroyer in the United States Navy, the first ship named for Rear Admiral James A. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.body: The top 100 novels of all time published in English, as voted for by authors, critics and academics worldwide. How many have you read?

items.body: Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: New Caledonia is first sighted by Europeans, during the second voyage of Captain James Cook.
items.body: New Caledonia is a French territory consisting of a group of islands in the southwest Pacific Ocean, 220 km (140 mi) southwest of Vanuatu and 1,210 km (750 mi) east of Australia. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Treaty of Alcáçovas is signed by the Catholic Monarchs of Castile and Aragon on one side and Afonso V and his son, Prince John of Portugal.
items.body: The Treaty of Alcáçovas was signed on 4 September 1479 between the Catholic Monarchs of Castile and Aragon on one side and Afonso V and his son, Prince John of Portugal, on the other side. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Godfather is a series of crime novels about Italian-American Mafia families, most notably the fictional Corleone family, led by Don Vito Corleone and later his son Michael Corleone.
items.body: The first novel, The Godfather, written by Mario Puzo, was released in 1969. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The Moon of Much Gladness is a fantasy novel by English writer Ernest Bramah, told by an unnamed narrator who may be Kai Lung, a fictional itinerant story-teller of ancient China from other books by Bramah.
items.body: It was first published in hardcover in London by Cassell and Company, Ltd. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Mark Spitz becomes the first competitor to win seven medals at a single Olympic Games.
items.body: Mark Andrew Spitz is an American former competitive swimmer and nine-time Olympic champion. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Peter III of Aragon is proclaimed King of Sicily in Palermo.
items.body: Peter III of Aragon was King of Aragon, King of Valencia, and Count of Barcelona from 1276 to his death. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Nasreddin in Bukhara is a 1943 Soviet comedy film directed by Yakov Protazanov, based on the novel by Leonid Solovyov Disturber of the Peace about Nasreddin.
items.body: Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: World War II: William J. Murphy commands the first Royal Air Force attack on Germany.
items.body: World War II, or the Second World War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers. The world is stranger than it lets on.
